items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had learned all these Wayne Shorter solos... the Miles band was kind of our band.

ctx.x: Yeah, sure. When I was playing in Wynton’s band and I really…. I wasn’t really a jazz musician, I was playing jazz, but I didn’t know what the hell I was doing. But I had learned all these Wayne Shorter solos and we were working out of the mode, the Miles band was kind of our band. So I would play these really long solos that never really went anywhere and everything was like an inside joke. Because it was the band, we knew what was going on, the audience was sitting there going, “Ok. Where is this shit going?”…

Charlie Parker and those guys went through when the medium, you got one chorus, two tops. And they were all influenced by swing music, and in swing music they didn’t have those big long-ass solos like they have now. You know, post-Coltrane, you know.
